scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship - Bioceb (European Master in Biological and Chemical Engineering for a Sustainable Bioeconomy)

eligibility: Holds a Bachelor of Science (BSc) or equivalent
Proficiency in English, evidenced by a certificate
Has not previously obtained an Erasmus Mundus scholarship
Applications may come from all over the world, subject to the geographical balance rule
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to applicants from all over the world who hold a BSc or equivalent, with English proficiency and a full set of application documents. Previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders are not eligible for an additional award.
benefits: EUR 1,400 per month for travel, visa, installation and subsistence
Maximum total award of EUR 33,600 per student
A monthly scholarship or salary from the host company if the master's thesis is done as a paid company internship
coverage: Subsistence allowance of EUR 1,400 per month covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs
Award for the entire programme duration, pro-rata of actual days, maximum 24 months
Maximum value of EUR 33,600 per student
requirements: Upload every required document to the online application tool, including translations
Validate the application, since only validated applications are considered
Do not send any document by post or email
Apply for the EMJM scholarship with the same form and at the same time as the Bioceb programme application
documents: Copy of the Bachelor of Science (BSc) or equivalent
Copy of the high school diploma and/or transcripts of records or equivalent
Official documents for the past five years not covered by the last diploma
If needed, supporting documents for special needs or for socio-economic, social or political vulnerability
existing.english_requirement: Proof of English proficiency is a required application document.
application_method: Online application tool; an application folder can be started and completed later
existing.selection_notes: Bioceb is entitled to grant 50 EMJM scholarships across the whole project duration, approximately 12 per cohort, and states that a geographical balance must be ensured so that no more than 10% of the total scholarships awarded during project implementation go to candidates of the same nationality.
existing.best_fit: Applicants worldwide with a BSc in a chemical, biological or process engineering field who need tuition, mobility and living costs covered for a two-year bioeconomy Master's.
existing.notes: EMJM scholarships are available for the next four cohorts. The consortium is Aalto University (Finland), AgroParisTech (France), Universite de Liege (Belgium), TalTech (Estonia) and Universite de Reims Champagne Ardenne (France).
existing.application_period: 3 November 2026 11:30 Paris CET to 19 January 2027 11:30 Paris CET
existing.deadline_display: Application period: November 3rd, 2026, 11:30 a.m. (Paris CET) to January 19th, 2027, 11:30 a.m. (Paris CET). The window opens after this verification on 2026-10-04.
existing.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree Programme scholarship

scholarships.title: France-South Africa Scholarship Programme 2027
scholarships.official_source: Embassy of France in South Africa (France Excellence Scholarship)

existing.description: The Embassy of France in South Africa invites citizens of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi to apply for Master's or PhD study at French higher education institutions in the 2027/28 academic year under the France Excellence scheme. Successful applicants receive a monthly living allowance, one return economy-class airfare, social security and health insurance, priority access to student accommodation and exemptions from the visa fee and the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC). Tuition fees are not covered by the scholarship. Because of the opposing hemispheres' academic calendars, laureates follow online French-language courses through the Alliances Françaises network in South Africa from February to July 2027 before departing for France in September 2027.
eligibility: Be a citizen of South Africa, Lesotho or Malawi
Be born on or after 1 January 1997
Have obtained a minimum average of 60% in their most recently completed qualification
Intend to pursue a Master's or PhD at a recognised higher education institution in France
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of South Africa, Lesotho or Malawi, born on or after 1 January 1997, without dual French citizenship, with a minimum 60% average in their most recently completed qualification, intending to study at a recognised higher education institution in France.
benefits: Monthly living allowance of EUR 900 for Master's students
Monthly living allowance of EUR 1,850 for PhD students
Exemption from the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC)
Eligibility to apply for additional housing assistance through the French Family Allowance Fund (CAF)
coverage: Monthly living allowance of EUR 900 (Master's) or EUR 1,850 (PhD)
Exemption from the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC)
requirements: Master's applicants: up to three preferred study programmes with programme web links, application dates and tuition fees
PhD applicants: a prospective French supervisor or research laboratory identified before applying
PhD applicants: research proposal of 2-3 pages
PhD applicants: timeline for research periods in France where applicable
Optional supporting documents: recommendation letters, language certificates, cost-sharing commitments
application_method: Applications must be submitted online only via the dedicated France-South Africa Scholarship Programme platform
Applicants must complete the Final Submission before the closing date
Incomplete or late applications will not be considered
Applicants must not contact the scholarship panel regarding application status
existing.best_fit: South African, Lesothoan or Malawian citizens under 30 with a 60% or better average who hold or will hold a Master's or are starting a PhD in France and can meet the French-language preparatory track in South Africa.
existing.notes: Funding period: per month for Master's students (EUR 1,850 per month for PhD students)
existing.duration: Master's: duration of the degree (typically 2 years); PhD: up to 3 years
existing.application_period: Applications opened 21 July 2026 and closed 8 October 2026 23:59 South Africa time; interviews in November 2026 and shortlisted candidates announced in early December 2026.
existing.deadline_display: Application deadline: 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa time)
